thesis: Existing earnings and CFO strengthen the recovery case beyond management guidance, but neither side has medical-cost and reimbursement evidence sufficient to price the upcoming test. Neutral treats October13 as information risk rather than a favorable catalyst or already-missed target. Cash conversion does not settle claims sensitivity or owner cash after investment.
strongest_counterexample: $8.0bn operations earnings and $11.1bn CFO,1.9times net income, provide strong current evidence in addition to the raised $19.50–$20.00 adjusted-EPS outlook.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent primary update lowers FY adjusted-EPS outlook below its current $19.50 lower bound, invalidating the retained raised-outlook recovery scenario.

Actual subsequent cost/utilisation disclosure supports delivery of the stated outlook with positive post-investment cash and funded obligations, resolving major cost/funding gates and requiring reassessment.
evidence_gaps: Medical utilisation, reimbursement and sustainable costs.
Owner cash after investment and debt-service capacity.
Matched valuation of event risk and actual guidance delivery.
decisive_factors: 4.9% net margin creates claims sensitivity without a supplied cost bridge.
Debt/capital41.2% is relevant, not proof of distress.
October13 results not yet delivered; stabilisation belowSMA-50 is incomplete.
